summary: A UGREEN blog article titled 'The Ultimate Guide to Eco-Friendly Furniture: Sustainable Choices for a Greener Home' that explains what eco-friendly furniture is, why to choose it, which materials and certifications to look for, and how to care for, buy, DIY, dispose of and understand the trends in sustainable furniture. It also recommends several eco-furniture brands and promotes UGREEN's own sustainable interior design course. Most of the page is boilerplate such as navigation, newsletter prompts, cookie notices and footer text, which was ignored.
one_line: A UGREEN guide covering materials, certifications, brands, costs, care, DIY and disposal for eco-friendly furniture in a greener home.
key_facts: The article is published by UGREEN and is dated February 16 in the page header, under the Sustainability category.
The guide names three core principles of eco-friendly furniture: Sustainability, Ethical Manufacturing, and Longevity and Durability.
FSC Certified stands for Forest Stewardship Council and is described as the gold standard for wood.
GREENGUARD certification focuses on indoor air quality and certifies that furniture emits low levels of volatile organic compounds (VOCs).
Oeko-Tex Standard certification applies to textiles and guarantees that fabrics are free from harmful chemicals.
The brands listed as pioneers of green living in 2024 are Green Furniture Concept, EcoBalanza, and West Elm.
West Elm is described as a well-known brand offering a wide range of FSC-certified products.
The sustainable materials list includes bamboo, reclaimed wood, recycled metals and plastics, and organic fabrics.
The article says the myth that eco-friendly furniture automatically means more expensive is just that, a myth.

The cost comparison table rates eco-friendly furniture as higher initial cost, longer longevity, and positive health and environmental impact, versus lower initial cost, shorter longevity, and negative impact for traditional furniture.
The DIY ideas are a pallet coffee table, wine crate shelves, and milk crate storage, with the pallet coffee table and wine crate shelves rated Beginner level.
The article lists three future trends: biodegradable materials, smart furniture, and local sourcing.
Responsible disposal options listed are recycling, donation, and repurposing.
The article promotes a sustainable interior design course with the call to action 'I Want to Learn More'.
The page advertises an in-person event, Green Interiors Day in Milan on April 15th.
